text.p: By Peter Campbell*
WITTEY OUTSAILS CONNER IN U.S.

Back in the early 1900s when that famous Irish tea merchant SIR THOMAS LIPTON was attempting to wrest the America's Cup from the New York Yacht Club, he presented a magnificent trophy for competition between yacht clubs in North America.

Since then it has become one of the most prestigious events on the U.S. sailing calendar and last weekend saw the 82nd contest for the Sir Thomas Lipton Cup sailed off Newport Beach, California, with the Balboa Yacht Club defending it for the fifth time against 16 challengers from clubs in the U.S. and Canada.

The winner was the Coronado Cays Yacht Club across the bay from San Diego, but the winning skipper was an Australian -- champion Sydney yachtsman NEVILLE WITTEY, who has been a member of the club since the 1995 America's Cup when he steered SYD FISCHER's boat in some of the challenger races.

Among the leading Americans WITTEY outsailed was America's Cup 2000 challenger DENNIS CONNER, who put in a big effort to win the historic Cup, including buying the winning yacht of the past few years and investing in the latest state-of-the-art sails.

"We had two wins, a third, a fourth and a sixth in the series, sailed in Shock 35 cruiser/racers, and beat CONNER in all but one of the five races," an elated WITTEY told Reuters on Thursday after returning from the U.S.
"In the second last race he tried to match race us down the fleet and in the final race it was a full-on match race start -- but we pushed him over the line early."

WITTEY, the 1996 Yngling class world champion and the most successful Etchell keelboat sailor on Sydney Harbour last summer, heads overseas again shortly on a European campaign in the Olympic Soling class.
With JOSHUA GRACE and DAVID EDWARDS as crew, he will contest Kiel Week in Germany, the Italian Open, the Danish Open and then the 1997 World championship in Denmark in June and July.
LATE BID FOR AUSSIE WHITBREAD BOAT

Last minute efforts are being made to have an Australian-sponsored and crewed yacht in the Whitbread round the world race. Entries officially closed on June 1 but with only ten new W60s built for the 1997-98 race, officials will accept late entries over the next few weeks.

So far nine new Whitbread 60s have been launched (a U.S. boat will be launched shortly) but according to Whitbread headquarters there are syndicates from Australia, South Africa, France and Belgium hoping to secure second-hand W60s. At least one of the challenging syndicates, Merit Cup representing Monaco with New Zealander GRANT DALTON as skipper, has built two new boats and one might be available to the Australians.

The hopes of building a new boat in Sydney for the Elle Racing syndicate appear to have foundered but 18-footer sailors MICHAEL SPIES (also a vastly experienced ocean racing sailor) and DAVID WITT are still confident of gaining sponsorship and a boat.

Many of the new Whitbread 60s will be seen in action as a fleet in the Fastnet Race in August, sailing the same course as the Admiral's Cup team yachts and other entries, but continuing on back to Cowes after crossing the Plymouth finishing line.
ORD MINNETT LAUNCH INTO YACHTING

The investment house Ord Minnett have launched into yachting, this week announcing their sponsorship of one of Sydney's most significant offshore regattas -- Middle Harbour Yacht Club's Short Ocean Racing Championship, now in its 17th year.

The support from Ord Minnett, one of Australia's leading stockbroking and financial services houses -- and this year celebrating 125 years in business -- comes at a time when intense interest is being focused on Sydney leading up to the 2000 Olympics.
This is believed to be the first time that Australian yachting has received sponsorship from a major company in the financial sector, although there has been support for individual yachtsmen.

The four-race Ord Minnett Short Ocean Racing Championship, to be known simply as the Ord Minnett Regatta, will be sailed off Sydney Heads over the weekend of 29 and 30 November 1997, with divisions for IMS, PHS and JOG rated yachts.

Significantly, it is expected that the regatta, previously called the Bruce & Walsh Regatta, will be used as the selection series for teams to represent Australia, New South Wales and Clubs in the Telstra Southern Cross Cup international series in December.

Last year's Short Ocean Racing Championship attracted an elite fleet of ocean racers, with SYD FISCHER'S Kenwood Cup winner Ragamuffin taking out the IMS Racer Division from WARWICK MILLER'S Exile and Atria, owned by Gold Coast based heart surgeon GILBERT FORD.

Queensland champion No Fearr, skippered by young Townsville businessman CAREY RAMM won the IMS Cruiser Racer Division from Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron member IVAN WHEEN'S Zoe and Bashfull, skippered by Cruising Yacht Club vice-commodore and property developer HUGO VAN KRETSCHMAR.
In the PHS Division, ROB REYNOLD'S J44 Phoenix won a hardfought series with her sistership Adria, skippered by CHRIS GORMAN.
AMERICA'S CUP, ADMIRAL'S CUP REUNIONS
There will be many a tall story of yachting told by some old timers at two reunion dinners planned for the week after next.
On Wednesday, June 18, an Admiral's Cup Reunion Dinner will be held at the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron to celebrate Australia's first victory at Cowes 30 years ago.
It's been organised by former Admiral's Cup yachtsman PETER HEMERY and is expected that some of the greats of Australian ocean racing will be there.
On Saturday, June 20, there will be a reunion dinner for the crew and support team of the 1977 America's Cup Challenge by Gretel II at Noakes Boatshed, Berry's Bay -- black tie and all.

The theme of that challenge, with the timber Gretel II and her crew older than most at Newport, Rhode Island, was "Daughters of America...lock up your Mothers." For the reunion dinner it's "Daughters of America...lock up your Grandmothers!" I guess that most of the comely lasses of Newport, Rhode Island, I met that year in the Candy Store and other establishments with the Gretel II team are now well and truly grandmothers!
1997 ADMIRAL'S CUP CHALLENGERS IN ACTION

Australia's 1997 Admiral's Cup team is already in action in Europe, with advertising agency head STEVE KULMAR and product promotions expert RICHARD FRIEDRICHS and their crew sailing Sea in the Mumm 36 world championships at Punta Ala, Italy, this week in preparation for the Cowes event in July/August.

Going into the long seventh race, the Australians were in ninth place overall in the top calibre fleet, placing in the top ten in all but one race, including an excellent third in race four and placing sixth in two other races.

Unfortunately, the Aussies went the wrong way in the flukey light weather race across the Mediterranean to the coast of North Africa and early today crossed the line in 11th place, dropping them back to 11th in overall standings after seven of the 11 races. But they weren't the only ones to falter -- second placed British boat Bradamante (the Mumm 36 in the British Admiral's Cup team) finished stone motherless last, slipping to fifth in standings.

The fleet has attracted a star-studded line-up of the world's top yachtsmen, including America's Cup sailors and Olympic medallists, with the German yacht I Punkt, steered by New Zealander GAVIN BRADY, finishing second in the long race to hold a clear overall lead.
*Peter Campbell is editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
